links.caveat: On 64-bit builds lambda <= 64, so root_u = lambda/131072 = 0 and public inputs take the finite-size fallback. Nothing here exercises the recursive subexponential kernel. ic.tensor_contraction_v1 is an exponential toy (protocol H1).
links.isolation_reason: L0 ('recorded') is the level ecbench documents as sufficient for operation counts, which do not depend on contention; it is the lowest level the spec schema accepts. The EKS L2 gate refuses these panels because rho solves at 10-16 bits take under 1 ms (MIN_SOLVE_WALL_NS_V3 = 1,000,000 ns grades them L1; run gh-41008826427-1: 176/192 L1; exit 42). A counts-only session needs no wall isolation. Run with `ecbench run --cpus none` (L0 by construction) and a per-track --lock path if the tracks run concurrently.

changes_from_originals: GATE-FORCED (both tracks): isolation_required L2 to L0. On EKS the run-ecbench L2 gate grades any solve under 1 ms as L1 (record.rs MIN_SOLVE_WALL_NS_V3) and exits 42; rho at 10-16 bits solves in microseconds (run gh-41008826427-1: 176/192 records L1). L0 is the level ecbench documents as sufficient for operation counts.

DISCRETIONARY, filed before data: rounds, C 10-14 bits 6 to 1 and B 5 to 1. S is a deterministic function of (workload, algorithm seed) and replays exactly; more rounds would add new walk seeds per target (power), which P1 and P4 do not need at their expected effect sizes. Cost: C3 (tensor vs ic-mitm) and B-source-selectors are probably underpowered at one round (sample_size.power), so no_ranking is the expected outcome there and is not evidence of parity. The C 16-bit spec already had 1 round.

DISCRETIONARY, filed before data: warmup 1 to 0 on all three specs. A warm-up only absorbs one-time wall costs, which counted S does not see; the measured round then uses absolute algorithm-seed index 0, which no measured round of the originals used.

DISCRETIONARY, filed before data: C order alternate to alternate_measured on 10-14 bits. With warmup 0 and one round both orders run the single round in spec order, so the plan's execution order is identical; alternate_measured matches the 16-bit original and avoids ecbench's warning that alternate parity counts warm-ups.

REVERTED in v2: v1 merged the two C specs into one with timeout_seconds 1800, which raised the 10-14-bit per-execution timeout from 900 s. v2 keeps two C specs as the originals do: 10/12/14 bits with timeout_seconds 900 (as tensor-ic-vs-rho.json) and 16 bits with 1800 (as tensor-ic-vs-rho-16.json). v1's statement that per-execution timeouts were unchanged was false for C; the 1800 s in the original C protocol is its job limit (execution.timeout_seconds), not a per-execution budget. In v2 every per-execution timeout equals its original's.
links.timeout_note: timeout_seconds is a wall-clock limit (runner.rs L1245: Duration::from_secs(timeout_seconds)). At L0 whether a row ends verified or timeout depends on the host, most of all for B's 30 s native rows; the C budgets are 900 s (10-14 bits) and 1800 s (16 bits). A timeout row is host censoring: unknown, never evidence that a method fails, and never a determinism failure.

question: On the registered bench-roster prime curves of 10, 12, 14 and 16 bits, what do ic.tensor_contraction_v1 (m = 2) and the four native hashed-base backends of ic.hashed_native_v1 cost in ecbench's counted unit S, how far is each from the matched rho.negation reference (distance remaining, per curve, across the AGENTS.md 5a pricing band), and how does median S scale with r? Counted S only; no wall time.

claims.text: Every planned execution of both specs is retained: verified scalar, or an explicit wrong_answer/timeout/exhausted/error outcome; a budget limit is unknown, never a nonexistence result.

Track C, per curve: the paired ratio of summed S, tensor-m2 over rho-neg (the distance remaining to rho), with compare's linearised_t interval (primary) and cluster-bootstrap interval (descriptive) at weights 0, 0.1 and 1 (the 5a band).
claims.if_supported: a measured counted-S gap to rho on these four toy curves
claims.if_not_supported: no ranking on that curve; the ratio is still reported as the distance remaining

claims.text: Track C, per curve: the paired ratio of summed S, tensor-m2 over ic-mitm (the current prime-curve IC baseline), with the 5a band. A ratio below 1 across the band would be an improvement over the IC baseline on that curve.
claims.if_supported: a measured counted-S difference from the IC baseline on these curves
claims.if_not_supported: no ranking against the IC baseline

claims.text: Log-log slope of median S (and of median total GAE) against log2 r for every arm with all 8 rows verified on at least three sizes, reported descriptively with its points and a target-resampled bootstrap interval.
claims.if_supported: a fitted exponent on four toy sizes, labelled an extrapolation outside them
claims.if_not_supported: fewer than three complete sizes: points only

claims.text: Track B, per curve and native backend: the paired ratio of summed S lower bound over rho-neg, with the 5a band, only on curves where that backend and rho-neg verified all 8 targets. Native S is a lower bound, so only 'costs more than rho' can be concluded; a ratio below 1 is reported as unranked. Because timeout_seconds (30 s) is wall-clock, which (backend, curve) cells are complete depends on the host.
claims.if_supported: a counted lower-bound gap to rho on these curves
claims.if_not_supported: incomplete or below-1: census and descriptive ratio only, no ranking

claims.text: Track B, per curve: native-source against native-selectors on complete verified pairs, with the 5a band (the original protocol's exploratory comparison).
claims.if_supported: a backend difference in counted lower-bound S on these curves

claims.text: Determinism: rho-neg and rho-neg-aa (both tracks) and native-selectors and native-selectors-aa (track B) share each (workload, round) algorithm seed, so on every pair whose two rows are both verified or both exhausted their S and total_gae must be identical, and ecbench verify --replay-all must reproduce every row. A status mismatch involving timeout is host censoring, not a determinism failure.
Wall time, speedups, asymptotic or subexponential behaviour, deployed-size curves, challenge scalars and full arithmetic pricing of the native arms are outside this protocol.

hypotheses.statement: The tensor arm costs far more than rho in S on every curve, and the gap grows with r (carried unchanged from crypto-ecdl-tensor-ic-speed-20261030).
hypotheses.mechanism: Each relation is found by exact contraction costing about |F_1||F_2| ~ 2r point additions, and N + 1 ~ 2(2r)^(1/2) relations are needed, so total GAE grows like r^(3/2) and S = GAE/sqrt(r) like r; rho's S is about 1 (total GAE like sqrt(r)).

predictions.minimum_effect: tensor-m2/rho-neg ratio interval above 1 on every curve, increasing from 10 to 16 bits

hypotheses.statement: With root_u = 0 every native hashed backend runs the finite-size fallback, so on every curve where a backend verifies all 8 targets its summed S lower bound exceeds rho-neg's at every 5a weight.
hypotheses.mechanism: No recursive subexponential kernel is reached at lambda <= 64; the fallback's bounded searches and checked group calls are exponential in the curve size, while rho needs about sqrt(pi r/4) additions.

power.note: Computed by analysis/decide.py power (no data). Family: C-rho, C-ic (4 curves each) + B-rho-{source,selectors,width,partial,ic} and B-source-selectors (4 curves each) = 32 per-curve tests; Holm at alpha 0.05, so the strictest step tests at 0.05/32 = 0.0015625 and the loosest at 0.05. Each cell has 8 paired targets, df 7; t_crit = 5.0016 (0.05/32 two-sided) and 2.3646 (0.05). Model (assumption, not data): se(ln R) ~ sqrt(cv_A^2 + cv_B^2)/sqrt(8), rho cv ~ sqrt(4/pi - 1) = 0.523 (Rayleigh-like collision time). Minimum detectable ratio at power ~0.5 (~0.8), first Holm step / last step: rho vs a deterministic-cost arm 2.52 (2.98) / 1.55 (1.83); rho vs an arm with cv 0.25 2.79 (3.35) / 1.62 (1.95); rho vs an arm with rho-like spread 3.70 (4.68) / 1.86 (2.35); IC vs IC with both cv 0.25 1.87 (2.09) / 1.34 (1.50); with both cv 0.5 3.49 (4.37) / 1.81 (2.26). P1 (tensor/rho, expected to grow like r, so far above these on every curve) and P4 (native lower bound/rho, expected far above 1) are powered under this model. passes is false because the family is not uniformly powered: C3 (tensor vs ic-mitm) and B-source-selectors have no expected effect size above these thresholds, so C3 is probably underpowered at one round and no_ranking is the expected outcome there; it is not evidence of parity. C-rho-ic, C-aa, B-aa-* and B-pos are reported but are not in the family. Rounds and warmup are discretionary changes (links.changes_from_originals).

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Scaled from the 2026-10-30 session-log sizing (contended host): tensor solve 12 bits 3 s, 14 bits 21 s, 16 bits about 417 s; 10 bits assumed <= 1 s. Track C, two sessions: C-small (10/12/14 bits, 96 executions) tensor 8 x (1 + 3 + 21) s ~ 200 s plus 72 rho/rho-aa/ic-mitm rows at ~1 s; C-16 (32 executions) tensor 8 x 417 s ~ 3340 s (0.93 h, each well inside the 1800 s per-execution timeout) plus 24 rows at ~1 s; C total ~3.7e3 s (~1.0 h). Track B: 288 executions; worst case every native row (160) runs to its 30 s budget, 4800 s, plus 128 sub-second rows; B upper bound ~4.9e3 s (~1.4 h). Sequential worst case ~8.7e3 s (2.4 h); the tracks may run concurrently on separate CPUs (counts are contention-independent, but contention can turn a native row into a wall-clock timeout, which censors it), about 1.4 h wall.

primary.name: S
primary.definition: every phase charged in ecbench.gae divided by sqrt(r); a lower bound for the native arms, whose arithmetic is not completely priced. Interval: ecbench compare's linearised_t (delta-method ratio-of-totals interval, targets as clusters, Student t(7), log scale) is primary; the cluster bootstrap (4000 resamples, seed 20261002) is descriptive; the uncertainty enum below is the nearest schema value

secondary.name: unpriced native work
secondary.definition: every *_uncharged counter on every arm, rho included, priced at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per operation for the 5a band (ecbench band --weights 0,0.1,1; ecbench compare --weight w)

secondary.name: outcome census
secondary.definition: count of verified / wrong_answer / timeout / exhausted / error rows per arm and curve, with the exclusive phase where incomplete native attempts stopped

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: C-small 4 arms x 24 workloads x 1 round = 96 executions and C-16 4 arms x 8 workloads x 1 round = 32 executions (C total 128); B 9 arms x 32 workloads x 1 round = 288 executions; no warm-up; then stop

per-execution budgets are the specs' and equal the originals' (C 900 s on 10/12/14 bits, C 1800 s on 16 bits, B 30 s, all wall-clock; and every native call's 5M-step bound); a row that hits them is retained as unknown (timeout) or exhausted, never rerun with a larger budget
a row whose answer does not verify stops nothing and is recorded as wrong_answer

invalidation_rules: a row with outcome.status other than verified is excluded from ratios and slopes and reported in the census
a session whose ecbench verify --replay-all is not OK with every replay identical yields no result for its track

a determinism control (C-aa, B-aa-rho, B-aa-selectors) invalidates its track's counted results only when S or total_gae differs on a (workload, round) pair whose two rows are both verified or both exhausted

a status mismatch in a determinism pair that involves timeout is host/infrastructure censoring (timeout_seconds is wall-clock, runner.rs L1245): the affected cell becomes incomplete_unknown; it is not a determinism failure and not a negative result
B is invalid if B.rho-neg-v2 fails to verify any target

no curve-level ratio containing a censored pair (timeout or exhausted, compare.rs run_cost) is used for ranking or for P1/P4; such a ratio is shown only as descriptive and flagged incomplete_unknown, a ratio containing a timeout pair is not shown at all, and no wall-implied S figure is reported
any wall-time number from these sessions is descriptive host timing and is never reported as a result

decision_rule.text: Implemented by analysis/decide.py (frozen with this protocol; sha256 in analysis_plan.script). Per (comparison, curve) cell, A the denominator arm and B the numerator: (1) at each weight w in {0, 0.1, 1} GAE per unpriced operation on every arm, rho included, run `ecbench compare --dir SESSION --a A --b B --weight w --resamples 4000 --seed 20261002 --json` and read curves[slug]: R_w = ratio_b_over_a (sum S(B)/sum S(A) over the 8 paired targets, reported as distance remaining R and log2 R) and the primary interval ci95 (ci_method linearised_t, df 7, log scale). The cluster bootstrap (ci95_bootstrap) is reported and decides nothing. (2) The cell is complete only if all 8 rows of both arms on that curve are verified and compare reports 8 pairs, 0 censored pairs and linearised_t at every weight; otherwise it is incomplete_unknown, gets p = 1, is never ranked and is never used for P1 or P4. (3) Per weight, cv_w = ln(hi_w/R_w)/t_{0.975,7}, T_w = ln(R_w)/cv_w, p_w = 2(1 - F_t7(|T_w|)). (4) Band condition: ln R_w has the same sign at all three weights and `ecbench band --weights 0,0.1,1 --ranks` gives the same order on that curve; band ranks supply only this 'order holds at 0, 0.1 and 1' condition (they compare point means and carry no interval). Failing it, p = 1 and no_ranking. (5) Native lower-bound arms (B-rho-source, -selectors, -width, -partial): only R > 1 is rankable. (6) Cell p = max over the three weights of p_w. (7) Holm over the 32 cells at alpha 0.05: sort p ascending (ties by comparison id, then log2 r); the k-th is ranked (supported_within_scope, with its direction) iff p_(j) <= 0.05/(32 - j + 1) for every j <= k; equivalently its two-sided interval at level 1 - 0.05/(32 - k + 1) excludes 1 on the same side at every weight. Every other cell is no_ranking or incomplete_unknown. P1 is supported_within_scope only if all four C-rho cells are ranked B > A and R increases from 10 to 16 bits at every weight. P4 is judged only on the complete native cells, a host-dependent set. C3 below 1 across the band would count as a measured improvement over the IC baseline; it is not expected, and at one round no_ranking is the expected C3 outcome (not parity). Slopes are OLS of log2 median S on log2 r over complete sizes, intervals by resampling targets within size (descriptive).
decision_rule.threshold: Holm step-down over 32 cells at alpha 0.05: cell p (max over weights 0, 0.1, 1 of the linearised_t two-sided p, df 7) <= 0.05/(32-k+1) at its step k, with the sign of ln R the same at all three weights and confirmed by ecbench band --ranks; native lower-bound arms rankable only for R > 1
decision_rule.statistic: ratio of summed S over the 8 paired targets per curve, B over A (ecbench compare curves[].ratio_b_over_a), with T = ln R / cv, cv backed out of compare's linearised_t log-scale ci95
decision_rule.interval: ecbench compare linearised_t (delta-method, targets as clusters, Student t(7), log scale; primary); cluster bootstrap with 4000 resamples, seed 20261002 (descriptive only); Holm step-down levels 1 - 0.05/(32-k+1)
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: ratio of summed S per curve (distance remaining to rho), and log-log slope
